items.title: Janet Harrop, Wellington Federation of Agriculture (OFA) provided
notes: background on the mandate of the federation, indicating their role is to advocate for members and protect and preserve agricultural land. She noted agriculture is the largest economic sector in the County contributing $841 million to Ontario’s GDP and based on Census data the OFA has shown that 319 acres of farmland is lost every day – nearly double the 175 acres/day in 2016.

Janet Harrop reviewed the checklist and land use principles to support agricultural growth in Centre Wellington and responded to questions regarding the establishment of an agricultural advisory committee and use of the Reference Guide related to backyard chickens, site alteration, normal farming practices, etc.

items.title: Anthea Fisher, expressed concerns with the transparency of the process
notes: and the legal non-conforming status related to parking. She expressed concerns with a change of use, as owners of property within a C1 zone, they would be required to provide half a parking space which they are unable to do. The current draft by-law also does not allow new STRs in a C1 zone without providing parking. She suggested Council consider a) deferring adoption of the zoning by-law amendment and the short term rental licensing by-law, b) hold an additional public meeting, c) consider permitting existing and future short term rentals in the downtown areas to be legal non-conforming, and 4) allow the parking requirements to be achieved with proof of parking arrangements.

items.title: Will Feenstra, Inner Joy Getaways expressed concerns with the extra
notes: costs associated with the proposed licensing by-law, the municipal accommodation tax, and provisions within the by-law that appear to prohibit an owner/operator from holding weddings, parties and events.

He noted the occasional use provisions within the zoning by-law allow activities not normally permitted to occur up to 28 times per year and questioned whether the provisions in the licensing by-law contradicts those occasional uses.

items.title: Erika Montero expressed concerns that residential units situated above
notes: commercial space can convert to a hotel without a planning or public process provided they meet the 6 room threshold and are not subject to licensing. She noted the Hotel Registration of Guests Act, RSO 1990 was designed to strengthen record-keeping for hotels (6+ rooms) to combat human trafficking and is in fact a law enforcement tool and not a land use planning tool. She suggested provisions be included to protect long term and short-term residential units above commercial space by not permitting residential dwelling units in the C1 zone to be converted to hotels without a zoning amendment and therefore a public process and council approval.

items.title: Glenn Rumdell expressed concerns with the process, citing confusion
notes: over what provisions were changed and is seeking clarification on the renewal process, the contents of the Renter’s Code of Conduct and the restrictions on the licensee to host weddings, parties or other events. He expressed concerns with the non-refundable and questions whether the occupancy provision of 2 persons per bedroom allowed for a baby.

items.title: Darcy Saunders expressed concerns regarding the absence of any
notes: existing regulations for short term rentals and bed and breakfasts and is supportive of the licensing by-law. He expressed concerns with the proposed zoning by-law amendment, in particular, the provision where a residential dwelling unit is a permitted use, a Bed and Breakfast establishment and short-term rental unit are permitted uses and shall be deemed to comply with the provisions of the zoning by-law so long as it continues to be used for that purpose.

items.title: Operating Results - December 31, 2025
notes: Report from M. Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer M. Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer provided an overview of the report, indicating the 2025 tax supported operating fund deficit is $51,433. He explained the deficit is largely due to unfavorable variances for winter control and related public works fleet expenditures due to poor winter conditions in 2025, and lower than anticipated investment income and planning revenue. These unfavorable variances were partially offset by positive variances for parks and recreation revenues; rebates and natural gas savings resulting from the elimination of the carbon tax in April 2025; supplementary taxation revenue net of write-offs; unfilled positions in various divisions; and interest and penalties revenue on property tax accounts in arrears.
M. Bradey responded to questions regarding winter control, and details regarding the cemetery budget.

items.title: Shuttle Bus Program Funding Update
notes: Report from K. Bettiol, Manager of Community Development K. Bettiol, Manager of Community Development provided an overview of the report, indicating the 2026 Shuttle Bus program is scheduled to begin May 15 to September 7, providing service every Friday, Saturday, Sunday, and on statutory holidays between downtown Fergus and downtown Elora. She noted the program was developed with the expectation that $20,000 in partnership funding would be secured to offset operating costs. Due to the withdrawal of a private partner sponsorship late in the planning process, only $10,000 in partnership funding has been secured.

K. Bettiol indicated Township staff is recommending proceeding with an award for shuttle services to allow the 2026 Shuttle Bus Program to proceed as the program supports transportation between downtown Fergus and downtown Elora during the peak tourism and event season.
The service also helps alleviate parking shortages, improve mobility, support access to local businesses and destinations, and contributes to a more convenient experience for visitors and residents.

items.title: EASE Grant Application - Bissell Park Multi-Use Pad Replacement
notes: Report from K. Beirnes, Manager of Buildings & Property K. Beirnes, Manager of Buildings & Property provided an overview of the report, indicating Intake 2 of the Ontario Enhancing Access to Spaces for Everyone (EASE) Grant was released on March 25, 2026, under the Ministry for Seniors and Accessibility. He noted this grant fund is available to municipalities and not-for-profit organizations to improve accessibility in communities and support active lifestyles for people with disabilities and older adults.

K. Beirnes explained the Bissell Park Multi-Use Pad replacement project will improve accessibility and increase barrier-free paths of travel so that the facility can be accessed and used by people of all ages and abilities.

Specifically, the project will include a new access ramp connecting the Bissell Park path to the multi-use pad, and a ramp connecting an existing park pavilion to the facility. In addition to pathways, the upgraded pad surface will provide a safe, accessible, and barrier free recreational space. K. Beirnes noted the project meets the eligibility criteria and is well-suited for the EASE Grant.

items.title: Community Planning Permit System (CPPS) Initiation
notes: Report from M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services

M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services indicated a Community Planning Permit System (CPPS) is a land use planning tool available to municipalities in Ontario as authorized under Section 70.2 of the Planning Act. It is intended as an alternative tool to help plan and shape the future of a community based on its own vision and objectives. She noted the process combines several typical planning application types, such as zoning by-law amendments, minor variances, and site plan approval into a single streamlined application and approval process with a 45 day turnaround instead of 180 days common with other application processes.

M. Iglesias outlined the key differences and benefits between the current system and the CPPS, the lessons learned from other municipalities, the intended scope of the request for proposal (RFP), timing of the project short term and long term, proceeding with a feasibility study initially, Discussion ensued and Members of Council discussed a phasing approach, additional committee of the whole meetings or workshops and revising the scope of the draft RFP.
Mayor Watters called for a 7 minute recess, the meeting resumed at 8:31 pm.

items.title: Update on Ontario's "Bring-Your-Own" at Outdoor Festivals and Events
notes: Framework

Report from A. Gilmore, Managing Director of Community Services K. Bettiol, Manager of Community Development indicated the Province of Ontario introduced a framework, titled “Bring-Your-Own” Alcoholic Beverages at Outdoor Public Events (herein referred to as the "BYO Framework"), allowing municipalities to opt-in to permitting attendees at designated outdoor festivals and events to bring their own alcohol for personal consumption within approved event areas. She noted participation in the BYO Framework is voluntary, requiring municipalities to formally opt-in by April 30, 2026 through passage of a participation by-law.

K. Bettiol indicated staff have reviewed the BYO Framework and considered its potential impacts on municipal operations, event management, public safety, and community standards and are recommending Centre Wellington not opt-in to the BYO Framework and staff will continue to monitor the implementation of this program in other municipalities and report back to Council should conditions or guidance change.

items.title: Short-Term Rental Accommodation and Bed and Breakfast
notes: Establishments Licensing update
Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer
Mayor Watters indicated in the interest of time and efficiency, the short- term rental licensing by-law and the associated proposed zoning by-law amendment will be combined and considered together.

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report, indicating the purpose of the report is to summarize and provide staff responses to the feedback received from ConnectCW, provide an update regarding the proposed amendments to the Township's zoning By-law, and obtain Council direction on next steps as it pertains to the licencing of Short-Term Rental Accommodations and Bed and Breakfast Establishments in Centre Wellington.

B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development provided background on the development of the draft zoning bylaw amendment, indicating the proposed zoning definitions for amendment added a new definition of "short-term rental accommodation" consistent with the draft licensing by-law, and also modified existing zoning hotel and motel. He explained Council heard from operators of existing short-term rental accommodations in commercial areas, raising a concern that the proposed by-law provisions would make their short-term rental use illegal and expressing a very clear desire that existing short-term rentals be permitted to continue as such and be protected from zoning regulations that would interfere with their continued use.

Staff and Paul Dray, Dray & Associates responded to questions regarding the change to the different definition of hotel and the inclusion of a general provision indicating where a residential dwelling unit is a permitted use as of April 27, 2026, an STR and Bed and Breakfast establishment per permitted uses and shall be deemed to comply with the provisions of the zoning bylaw so long as it continues to be used for that purpose.

Staff responded to additional questions regarding use of the zoning to assist with enforcement, uses associated with weddings, parties and events on properties with STRs or Bed and Breakfasts, compliance with zoning and parking provisions if establishments existed prior to the passing of the by-laws, enforcement approach, staff resources, and steps to address life safety concerns.

items.title: Municipal Accommodation Tax Update
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer indicated Council directed staff to bring forward a Municipal Accommodation Tax By-law for approval. Upon receipt of this direction, staff prepared a draft by-law detailing the framework of a Municipal Accommodation Tax and subsequently engaged the services of KML Municipal Consulting to perform a review, provide recommendations and a consolidated draft.
Councillor MacDonald indicated she would prefer to see a rate at 3.5% D. Wilson provided an overview of the rate analysis undertaken, indicating

a 5% rate supports the Township’s broader objectives related to the establishment of the Municipal Service Corporation and the reinvestment of MAT revenues into destination marketing, visitor servicing, and tourism-supported infrastructure. He noted the recommended rate strikes a balance between generating sufficient and stable funding to meaningfully advance tourism priorities while remaining proportionate, transparent, and aligned with best practices in Ontario.
